what: R030 D13: the ADR 0024 dynG-vs-dynG reading of e6e4cce (B) against e6f87ed (A)

diagnostics.what: the line graph's row build (the second hypergraph.build stage, ms, median of 6-8 interleaved rounds, coauth-DBLP, one heap layout, exclusive lock; $DYNG_SCRATCH/runs/r030-d13/ab/diag.py) of code variants built like the reading's sides

variants.fix: e6e4cce (side B): region_exceptions::run (the failed() check and a try block) per row
variants.v2: fix with flat_adjacency.cpp of base (only v2h_append guarded)
variants.v3: fix with run() reduced to the call (lambda kept; no check, no try)
variants.v4: fix with run() = try block only (no failed() check)
variants.v5: fix with run() = failed() check only (no try block)
variants.v6: parallel_chunks: dynamic chunks claimed by hand and one try block per thread (buffers padded to cache lines in its second reading)
variants.fb: the same sources built with -falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=32 -Wa,-mbranches-within-32B-boundaries (R020's flag set FB: the JCC-erratum mitigation)

diagnostics.reading: the try block per row costs 6-10 % in the release build and 0.3 % with the JCC-erratum mitigation flags: a code-placement effect on this CPU, not the cost of the code. In the release build v6 is faster than the per-row form on sequential (6076.7 against 6513.0 ms in the one session with both, 2.3 % above base) and slower than base on 8 threads (+8.1 %, padded +4.7 %; the per-row form was not in those sessions); with the mitigation flags on both sides the per-row form is within 0.3 % of base on both backends and v6 is 1.8 % (sequential) and 2.6 % (8 threads) above base. The per-row form is kept: it is the form that costs nothing once code placement is controlled, and v6's sequential gain in the release build does not hold on 8 threads (corrected on 2026-10-22 by the R030 review: this sentence said that v6 is not faster in the release build; ADR 0062)
